metadata.case_name: YU WAI KAN v. LAW CHO TAI

source: the orthopaedic diagnosis is compatible with soft tissue “whiplash injury”.
The Plaintiff complained of right sided neck/scapular and right waist pain, contusion of the back, shoulder and right temple, and right upper limb numbness.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain with neurological signs

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to the back / possible minor contusion to right side low back muscles
source: Dr Lam opines there was soft tissue injury to the back as well, and Dr Chun agrees there was possible minor contusion to right side low back muscles.
The Plaintiff complained of pin-pricking pain at right side low back.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of muscle, fascia or tendon of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

injuries.description: post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) caused by the Accident
source: he meets sufficient criteria for the diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder (“PTSD”)

it is common ground that the Plaintiff suffers from pre-existing bipolar disorder... On the other hand, although the collision was of moderate severity, it was certainly not trivial. It is reasonably arguable that the Accident has been a frightening experience for the Plaintiff. Even Dr Singer accepts that the Plaintiff has experienced significant stressors, including the Accident that is serious enough to threaten life or serious physical injury.

injuries.description: pre-existing bipolar affective disorder (bipolar II disorder since 2002)
source: he has also been suffering from pre-existing bipolar II disorder since 2002 with fair remission upon treatment.
he was diagnosed to suffer from bipolar affective disorder, and was maintained on mood stabilisers and regular psychiatric follow-up.

manifestations.description: limited range of neck movement / mild stiffness
flashbacks and nightmares of the Accident
persistent depressed mood, loss of energy, lack of motivation
fear of driving / avoidance of driving (phobia while driving)
reduced enjoyment of activities and social withdrawal

treatments_received: psychiatric medications (mood stabilisers, anti-depressants, lithium carbonate)
clinical psychological counselling (Dr Alice Wai-yee Kwok)
treatments_future: psychiatric and clinical psychology treatment (at least 2 years as provisionally estimated by Dr Ho)
desensitisation (exposure) therapy (Dr Singer: 8 sessions at two-week intervals for PTSD)
occupational therapy training at Rehabaid Centre / driver re-assessment

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities (physical injuries and psychiatric disabilities) - court found reasonable prospect of establishing PSLA
Pre-trial loss of earnings for the notional pre-trial period (30 months) - assessed at HK$428,160.00
Post-trial loss of earnings (assessed on a multiplier of 2 for 24 months) - assessed at HK$342,528.00

After the Accident, relationship with mother is 'so-so'; relationship with wife lukewarm; avoidance of baby daughter (eg he picked her up and threw her onto the bed; his wife then took the baby to live with her mother); inability/unwillingness to hold daughter for more than 3-5 minutes due to right waist pain
Spends most time at home, seldom goes out for walks or shopping, seldom goes on vacation, reduced interest in socialising and pastimes such as swimming and playing ball games

he meets sufficient criteria for the diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder (“PTSD”) it is common ground that the Plaintiff suffers from pre-existing bipolar disorder... On the other hand, although the collision was of moderate severity, it was certainly not trivial. It is reasonably arguable that the Accident has been a frightening experience for the Plaintiff. Even Dr Singer accepts that the Plaintiff has experienced significant stressors, including the Accident that is serious enough to threaten life or serious physical injury. he has also been suffering from pre-existing bipolar II disorder since 2002 with fair remission upon treatment. he was diagnosed to suffer from bipolar affective disorder, and was maintained on mood stabilisers and regular psychiatric follow-up.
